//: Reference ~/.shipd/drive/targets.json for /s:drive (shipd-drive, drive-targets-config). A repository may override entries by name in <content-dir>/drive/targets.json — only the named targets differ; entries this file declares and the repo file does not are inherited unchanged. Copy this file's shape to ~/.shipd/drive/targets.json and edit; the `//`-prefixed keys below are inert documentation, safe to keep or delete.
// authCacheTtlHours: Hours a cached login (~/.shipd/drive/auth/<target>.json) is reused before logging in again (drive-auth-cache). Default 8.
// default: The target name /s:drive assumes when the request names none and more than one target is configured; otherwise the skill lists targets as plain text and asks (drive-skill-flow).

targets.// targets: Each entry declares a url and an auth recipe of kind none, env, command, or manual.

auth.// kind=env: Reads two environment variables already set in the caller's shell, named by the `username` and `password` keys. The CLI never writes them to disk or to a worker's argv — only to the worker's environment.

auth.// kind=command: Runs the two argv arrays under the `username` and `password` keys and takes each secret from that command's stdout, trailing newline stripped. The `op item get` example below is one documented recipe built on the 1Password CLI — never a requirement; any command that prints a secret to stdout works.

auth.// kind=manual: No credential at all — a visible Chromium window opens at the url above and a person logs in by hand, which is the only way through MFA, SSO, a passkey, or an OAuth consent screen. drive.py resolves nothing and sets no login variable in the worker's environment. The storage state it captures is written to the same ~/.shipd/drive/auth/<target>.json cache every other kind writes, and reused under the same authCacheTtlHours TTL.
auth.// done: The completion signal that ends the wait, in the `wait` verb's grammar: a load state (load/domcontentloaded/networkidle), url:<pattern>, or a selector to wait for visible. Name a signal that only appears AFTER the login — one already true on the login page returns immediately. Omit it and the default rule applies instead: the wait ends once the URL has left the login page while the host still matches it, so a bounce through an identity provider's own domain does not end it early.
auth.// timeoutSeconds: How long to wait for that signal before giving up (default 300). On expiry the worker writes a debug screenshot beside the cache path, reports one Error: line, and leaves any previous cache untouched.
auth.// --manual: Any target, whatever its kind, can be logged into by hand with `drive.py login <target> --manual`. That flag also overrides a still-fresh cache, which is how you replace a cached login you know has gone bad.

auth.// kind=none: No login step — the session starts with no storage state.
